study.title: 1 Thessalonians 4 O Holiness, love and hope in the return of the Lord
study.overview: In this chapter, Paul goes from practical exhortations to pastoral consolation. First, he insists that the will of God is sanctification: believers must live in a holy way, especially in the area of sexual purity, remembering that rejecting this instruction is to reject God Himself. Then he deals with brotherly love, praising the church for already loving the brothers and encouraging her to grow even more, while calling her an orderly, quiet and productive life before the outside. Finally, he responds to anguish about those who died in Christ, affirming the hope of the resurrection and meeting with the Lord, and concludes with the call to mutual comfort.

outline.title: Living to please God in holiness
outline.explanation: Paul exhorts the brethren to progress in the Christian journey received from the apostles. The will of God is sanctification, which here includes abandoning sexual sin, controlling one's own body with honor and not harming others. The apostolic teaching is not only human counsel: rejecting it is to reject God, who also grants the Holy Spirit to empower this holy life.

outline.title: Brotherly love, quiet life and public witness
outline.explanation: The church had already been taught by God to love the brethren, and this was shown throughout Macedonia. Even so, Paul calls for continuous growth. He also guides believers to live with discretion, take care of their own affairs and work with their hands, so as to walk with respect to those outside and not depend on anyone.

outline.title: Hope for those who died in Christ
outline.explanation: Paul corrects hopeless sadness about those who died. The basis of Christian hope is the death and resurrection of Jesus: the dead in Christ will rise first, and the living will be gathered with them to find the Lord. The purpose of this doctrine is to comfort believers one another, not to feed speculation about the end.

study.context: The notes indicate that this section of the letter answers questions of the Thessalonians on various topics: sexual purity, love among Christians, fate of those who died and the time of the Lord's day. Paul writes with apostolic authority, linking his commandments to the Lord Jesus and to the teaching already received by the church. References to those outside suggest a Christian community living amidst unconverted, and mention of Macedonia shows a testimony that was already known beyond the local church.
study.theology: The chapter presents a Christian ethics centered on God's will, not moral speculation. Sanctification involves the body, desires and relationships, showing that faith reaches concrete life. Brotherly love is a sign of divine instruction and must grow continuously. Daily work also has spiritual value, as it supports an honest and respectable conduct. Christian hope, in turn, is anchored in the resurrection of Jesus and in the future meeting of his people with him; therefore, grief exists, but it is not hopeless. The Holy Spirit appears as the one who confirms and empowers this obedience.

scholarViews.insight: The will of God is sanctification, and this here includes turning away from sexual sin; rejecting this teaching is equivalent to rejecting God himself, who also gave the Holy Spirit to believers.
Paul begins to comfort those who wept for the dead in the Lord and seeks to dissuade them from excessive sadness, because Christians have a sure hope of resurrection.
Paul sends to live honestly, take care of his own affairs and work with his hands, to walk respectfully before those outside and not depend on anyone.

questions: In what ways does my concrete life show that I consider sanctification as the will of God, and not just as a religious idea?
Does my way of speaking and acting with other believers reveal brotherly love that already exists and that needs to grow more?
Does my way of facing the death of a believer reflects hope in the resurrection and meeting with the Lord, or just resignation?
study.practice: Choose a concrete practice for this week in each chapter block: to move away from any situation that feeds impurity; to make an intentional act of love for a brother or sister; and comfort someone bereaved with the hope of the resurrection into Christ, without turning the conversation into speculation about dates or details of the end.
study.uncertainty: The available notes do not explain in detail the expression about the "instrument" or "vae" in verse 4, nor allow us to safely affirm all possible senses of verse 6. It is also not possible to go beyond what the notes say about the exact way of the final meeting with Christ. Where there is more than one interpretation in commentators, I presented reading as an interpretation, not as an indisputable fact.
